title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $9.03 saw 10 and 7 units (vs baseline 7.6), indicating ~7% lift in sales is offset by price. No prior price increase at this level with known effect, so evidence is moderate.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.6. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased 2.3% to $9.03, above regular price $8.83. Historical data shows price increases correlate with demand drops: the two weeks at $9.03 (2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05) sold 10 and 7 units, vs baseline 7.6, implying a ~7% drop. Past promotions show mixed effects, but none at this price or with 2.3% increase. The uplift model suggests no effect, but evidence shows price sensitivity. Adjust downward with medium confidence due to consistent post-price-increase dips. No seasonal or promotional drivers in target week.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 42.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 26.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
